walkthroughs.title: Sore throat with nasal symptoms

doorway: My throat is scratchy and sore, and my nose keeps running.
Vital signs are available on the chart.
Perform a focused history and physical examination, discuss your plan, and document only what you obtain.
Use the time limit stated for your selected practice mode.

plan.notice: Use viral, allergic and exposure clues without reflex antibiotic treatment.
plan.pivot: Are symptoms linked to a cold contact, itching/sneezing, or a workplace exposure?
plan.exam: Use the supported case-specific maneuvers and document their actual findings; do not infer normal findings from the generic model.
plan.avoid: Treating an unperformed examination or a possible diagnosis as obtained fact.

goals: Use viral, allergic and exposure clues without reflex antibiotic treatment.
Document only supplied, asked or examined information.

My throat is scratchy and sore, and my nose keeps running.

timeline.patient: Yes. Swallowing stings about 4 out of 10, but I can drink normally.
timeline.why: Intensity and functional effect are distinct; record only the dimension answered.

timeline.student: When is the throat irritation worst?

timeline.why: Separate time since onset from duration of one episode and from continuity.

timeline.action: Clean hands, provide privacy and appropriate draping, explain the selected examination and help the patient into a comfortable position.
timeline.why: These are stated actions in this written example. A visual avatar does not verify hand hygiene, consent or hands-on technique.

timeline.finding: Well appearing, handling secretions and speaking comfortably.
timeline.why: Use the supported case-specific maneuvers and document their actual findings; do not infer normal findings from the generic model.

timeline.action: Auscultate heart — aortic, pulmonic, tricuspid, mitral, on skin
timeline.finding: Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
timeline.why: The course expects at least four listening posts, on skin.

timeline.action: Auscultate lungs — posterior, on skin, compare side to side, mouth open
timeline.finding: Clear bilateral breath sounds without wheeze.
timeline.why: The course expects six posterior fields, mouth open, on skin, comparing sides.

timeline.action: Inspect mouth and throat with light — tongue blade, oropharynx, tonsils
timeline.finding: Mild diffuse pharyngeal erythema with posterior cobblestoning; no tonsillar exudate, asymmetry or uvular deviation. Mouth opens normally.
timeline.why: This specific action releases only the finding shown here. Interpret it with the history; it does not confirm a diagnosis by itself.

timeline.action: Inspect nose with light source — right naris, left naris
timeline.finding: Bilateral pale mildly edematous turbinates with clear secretions.
timeline.why: This specific action releases only the finding shown here. Interpret it with the history; it does not confirm a diagnosis by itself.
This specific action releases only the finding shown here. Interpret it with the history; it does not confirm a diagnosis by itself.

timeline.action: Otoscopic exam of ears — right ear, left ear
timeline.finding: Both tympanic membranes intact and nonbulging.
timeline.why: This specific action releases only the finding shown here. Interpret it with the history; it does not confirm a diagnosis by itself.

timeline.finding: C3 bilateral paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
timeline.why: Name the level examined; findings are released by region.

timeline.student: The history and examination can help distinguish a cold, allergy and irritation from the new spray. We can relieve the soreness and reduce exposures. If drinking or breathing becomes difficult, seek urgent care.
timeline.patient: Thank you. I understand that the next steps depend on the examination and tests.
timeline.why: Proposed care, not a record of tests or treatment already completed.

timeline.student: What questions do you have about the next steps?
timeline.patient: I want to know what is causing this and how to get back to my usual activities.

timeline.student: We can discuss ventilation and a safer cleaning method with your workplace, with your permission.
timeline.patient: That would help. Thank you.
timeline.why: Answer the concern that was just expressed. Give a defensible recommendation and explain uncertainty; do not promise a diagnosis or recovery before the evidence supports it.

note.S:
CC: My throat is scratchy and sore, and my nose keeps running.

HPI: 31-year-old female. Four days of sore throat; rhinorrhea began 1 day earlier. Bilateral posterior throat discomfort. Scratchy/raw sensation without foreign-body sensation. Odynophagia 4/10; normal oral fluid intake. Worse in mornings and at end of cleaning shifts. Stable sore throat; rhinorrhea preceded it by 1 day. Daughter with URI; new workplace spray cleaner temporally provokes irritation. Dust/pollen-associated sneezing and ocular itching. Relief with warm fluids and avoiding spray. Acetaminophen 500 mg once; no antibiotics. Seasonal rhinitis history; greater throat discomfort now.

PMH: Seasonal allergic rhinitis; no other chronic illness.

PSH: No surgical history.

Meds: Loratadine 10 mg as needed; none this week.

SH: Never smoked or vaped. No alcohol. No recreational drugs. Office cleaner; variable ventilation. Lives with husband and 6-year-old daughter.

FH: Sister: allergic rhinitis; father: asthma. Mother: hypertension.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

ROS: Respiratory: Mild dry cough. No dyspnea. No wheeze. Heent: Clear rhinorrhea. Mild hoarseness. No otalgia. General: No reported fever. Mild fatigue. No chills. No drooling, trismus or inability to swallow liquids.
note.O:
Vitals: BP 110/68 mmHg, P 82 bpm, R 16 rpm, T 98.9 F oral, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 3", Wt 136 lbs

General: Well appearing, handling secretions and speaking comfortably.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
Lungs: Clear bilateral breath sounds without wheeze.
HEENT: Mild diffuse pharyngeal erythema with posterior cobblestoning; no tonsillar exudate, asymmetry or uvular deviation. Mouth opens normally.
HEENT: Bilateral pale mildly edematous turbinates with clear secretions.
HEENT: No tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy.
HEENT: Both tympanic membranes intact and nonbulging.
Osteopathic: C3 bilateral paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
A: 2. Allergic rhinitis with postnasal throat irritation
P: 1. Provide fluids and appropriate analgesia, and discuss infection-control measures. Clear viral features do not require routine streptococcal testing or antibiotics; test if the clinical pattern changes. Reassess if not improving within 5–7 days. Drooling, breathing difficulty, neck swelling or inability to swallow fluids needs urgent evaluation.

2. Resume appropriate rhinitis treatment, considering intranasal corticosteroid or a nonsedating antihistamine after review; teach spray technique and reduce identified allergen exposure. Explain that allergy may coexist with a cold and that antibiotics do not treat allergy.

3. Avoid direct aerosol inhalation, improve ventilation and review the product safety instructions with occupational health; do not mix cleaners. Consider safer work practices/products and explain prompt assessment for chest tightness or respiratory symptoms.

walkthroughs.estimate_method: 150 spoken words/minute plus the full simulation examination durations and 55 seconds for introductions and transitions; explanatory commentary excluded. This is a planning estimate, not a measured student performance.

reasoning.question: Are symptoms linked to a cold contact, itching/sneezing, or a workplace exposure?
reasoning.why: Use viral, allergic and exposure clues without reflex antibiotic treatment.
reasoning.if_present: Use the reported pattern to select the relevant examinations and assess urgency.
reasoning.if_absent: Keep alternatives open and ask a focused follow-up.
reasoning.document: Separate reported symptoms, observed signs, assessment and proposed care.

differentials.name: Viral pharyngitis
differentials.teaching_context: Acute URI exposure, rhinorrhea, cough and nonexudative throat support a viral illness.

differentials.name: Allergic rhinitis with postnasal throat irritation
aliases: Allergic rhinitis with postnasal throat irritation
differentials.teaching_context: Seasonal itching/sneezing, pale turbinates and cobblestoning support allergic contribution.

differentials.name: Inhalational irritant pharyngitis
differentials.teaching_context: New spray exposure with work-related worsening and relief away supports irritant contribution.

omissions: Explaining uncertainty and the practical follow-up plan.
